artists.biography:
The Strokes are an American rock band formed in New York City in 1998, consisting of Julian Casablancas (lead vocals), Nick Valensi (guitar, keyboard, backing vocals), Albert Hammond, Jr. (rhythm guitar, keyboard, backing vocals), Nikolai Fraiture (bass) and Fabrizio Moretti (drums, percussion).
Met with wide-spread critical acclaim, the Stroke’s 2001 debut, Is This It in 2001, helped ushered in the garage rock revival movement of the early-21st century—and ranks number four on Rolling Stone's 100 Best Debut Albums of All Time, number two on Rolling Stone's 100 Best Albums of the 2000s, and 199 on Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
While a number the Stroke’s members have embarked on a variety of side projects, the band regrouped for a fifth album, Comedown Machine, released on March 26, 2013. The Strokes have sold over 5 million albums to date.

apple_music.editorial_notes: At the start of the 2020s, when the 20-year nostalgia cycle caught up with The Strokes, their newfound teenage fans not only had the band’s undeniable first two albums to spin, but also the recently released The New Abnormal, a Grammy-winner produced by Rick Rubin. In the years since, The Strokes’ popularity has continued to grow—they even played right before Justin Bieber on Coachella’s main stage in 2026. On Reality Awaits, another Rubin collaboration, The Strokes return to their mid-period predilection for upending expectations and indulging bandleader Julian Casablancas’ creative impulses. Casablancas has always had a thing for vocal effects and here, he goes full tilt, employing AutoTune as a stylistic tool on multiple tracks. He also ad-libs in an over-the-top English accent a few times and repeats, “I’m a leech” over and over on “The Fruits of Conquest”. The many ingredients on album closer “Tyrants of the Mellow Moon” include Radiohead vibes, a brief ’80s-toned guitar solo and a Jim Morrison-esque spoken word outro. Lyrically, Casablancas wonders what to make of The Strokes’ refound relevance, knowing that any monument they make may eventually be forgotten. On “Going Shopping”, the album’s first single, he sings, “I’ve been thinking about what I wanna say/But I’m an old man, at least that’s what they tell me anyway.” Time will tell.

lastfm.wiki_content: Reality Awaits is the seventh studio album by the American rock band the Strokes. It is the band's first release since 2020's The New Abnormal. It was released on July 24, 2026. In a 2022 appearance on the Joe Rogan Experience podcast, producer Rick Rubin stated that he had been recording a new album with the Strokes in Costa Rica. The cover art for Reality Awaits, created by Johann Rashid, is based on the 1989 photograph (Untitled) Cowboy by Richard Prince. In April 6, 2026, the Strokes announced Reality Awaits via Instagram, with a teaser video displaying a 1980s Nissan 300ZX with text reading "In the flesh, it's even sexier", followed by the album's title and release date announced for June 26. On the same day, the band distributed cassette tapes containing the new song "Going Shopping" to 100 fans who had provided their mailing address to their promotional SMS service the previous week. They also debuted the song live at the Bill Graham Civic Auditorium. The following day, they revealed the album's cover art and released the track onto streaming platforms as the album's lead single. On May 13, the band released the second single "Falling Out of Love" on streaming platforms. On June 11, the band announced that the release date had been delayed to July 24. According to the review aggregator Metacritic, Reality Awaits received "generally favorable reviews" based on a weighted average score of 72 out of 100 from four critic scores. The review aggregator Any Decent Music gave the album a weighted average score of 6.5 out of ten from seven critic scores. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Reality Awaits is the seventh studio album by The Strokes, released via RCA Records and Cult Records. Following 2020’s The New Abnormal, it finds the band back with Rick Rubin as producer and a nine-song set that continues their blend of sharp guitar rock and tightly wound, melodic songwriting.

Early descriptions of the album suggest a more adventurous and unpredictable Strokes record, with reports pointing to looser structures, stylistic detours, and heavier use of Julian Casablancas’ vocal effects, including Auto-Tune as a creative device. The album’s rollout included the singles “Going Shopping” and “Falling out of Love,” and coverage described it as one of the band’s most experimental and internally varied releases to date.

Recorded in Costa Rica and completed across multiple locations, Reality Awaits keeps the classic Strokes lineup intact while pushing beyond the clean, angular indie-rock framework that made them famous. Its 41-minute runtime and concise track list preserve the band’s characteristic economy, but the surrounding commentary suggests a record that is stranger, freer, and more self-consciously restless than a straightforward comeback album.
